title: The Ethical Dilemma of the Deceptive Memory Study

questions.question: Case Background: Dr. Vance is investigating whether eyewitness memory can be altered using false feedback. Participants are told they are evaluating a culinary video, but an actor staged as a chef suddenly drops a knife and screams. Dr. Vance tells participants the chef lost a finger (which is untrue). Under APA standards, what is this experimental manipulation?

options.text: Active deception by commission
Passive deception by omission only
Naturalistic observation
Exempt educational demonstration

questions.explanation: Actively giving false, misleading factual information (that the chef lost a finger) constitutes active deception by commission.

questions.question: Two participants experience severe acute panic and begin hyperventilating upon seeing the knife drop. What is Dr. Vance's ethical responsibility under the principle of Beneficence?

options.text: Force them to continue so their panic data can be analyzed
Immediately halt the experiment for those participants, provide immediate care, and dehoax them
Wait until the full 60-minute session concludes before asking if they need water
Report the participants to the university disciplinary committee

questions.explanation: Beneficence and human subject protections require immediate intervention and termination of participation when acute psychological distress occurs.

questions.question: Dr. Vance wants to operationalize 'participant eyewitness accuracy'. Which operational definition is most concrete and objective?

options.text: The feeling of certainty the participant expresses in their heart
The number of correct details identified out of a 20-item standardized visual checklist
How believable the participant appears to the experimenter
A subjective rating of the participant's moral honesty

questions.explanation: Counting correct items on a standardized objective checklist provides an observable, quantitative, and reproducible operational measure.

questions.question: Dr. Vance hypothesizes that 'stress will distort memory, but if a participant has an unshakeable inner aura, their memory will be immune.' Why is this hypothesis scientifically flawed according to Karl Popper?

options.text: It is written in the present tense
The 'unshakeable inner aura' is an unfalsifiable construct that cannot be disproven
It requires the use of animals rather than humans
It uses more than 15 words

questions.explanation: Invoking an untestable, mystical construct like an 'unshakeable aura' creates a post-hoc loop that violates Popper's criterion of falsifiability.

questions.question: At the conclusion of the study, Dr. Vance reveals that the chef was an actor, the blood was syrup, and no injury occurred. What crucial debriefing process is this?

options.text: Dehoaxing
Stratified random sampling
Peer review
Latin square counterbalancing

questions.explanation: Dehoaxing is the debriefing phase where researchers disclose the true nature of experimental deceptions and correct false beliefs instilled during the study.

questions.question: Before conducting this study, Dr. Vance was required to submit the protocol to which regulatory body for human subjects review?

options.text: The Institutional Review Board (IRB)
The Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC)
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
The local city council

questions.explanation: Human participant research in academic institutions must be reviewed and approved in advance by the Institutional Review Board (IRB).
